name: Centaurus A halo, field S5 (Hubble)
blurb: A field in the outer halo of Centaurus A, along the stream of the dwarf galaxy CenA-MM-Dw3, which Centaurus A is tearing apart, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc5128s5-hubble
story: These scattered stars were pulled out of the dwarf galaxy CenA-MM-Dw3, the first dwarf found being tidally disrupted around Centaurus A. Its tidal tails stretch over 1.5 degrees across the sky.

claims.text: Centaurus A is a giant elliptical galaxy, also designated NGC 5128 (Cen A)
Hubble program 14259 followed up newly discovered substructures in the halos of NGC 253 and NGC 5128 to study their assembly histories
CenA-MM-Dw3 is the first tidally disrupting dwarf galaxy found around Cen A
CenA-MM-Dw3 has tidal tails spanning over 1.5 degrees
Dw3 NW is a region along the stream of CenA-MM-Dw3 at RA 13:23:57.6, Dec -41:42:00
The Hubble field NGC-5128-S5 is at RA 13 23 55.2, Dec -41 44 42 in the NGC 5128 halo
